weights.weightCitation: ESC 2019 Pulmonary Embolism Guideline (Konstantinides SV et al.); Wells DVT score; Davidson's Principles & Practice of Medicine 24th ed (2022). UNILATERAL acute painful leg swelling — Wells score + D-dimer/Doppler; the threat is propagation to PE (pleuritic chest pain, dyspnoea). Bilateral leg swelling is usually systemic, not DVT. Anticoagulate.

IDSA Skin & Soft Tissue Infection guideline; Davidson's Principles & Practice of Medicine 24th ed (2022). UNILATERAL red, warm, painful, swollen limb + fever; NECROTISING FASCIITIS (pain out of proportion, rapid spread, crepitus, systemic toxicity, skin necrosis) is a SURGICAL EMERGENCY needing urgent debridement — do not mistake for simple cellulitis.

ESC 2021 Heart Failure Guideline (McDonagh TA et al.); Davidson's Principles & Practice of Medicine 24th ed (2022). BILATERAL pitting oedema + orthopnoea/PND/exertional dyspnoea + raised JVP; UGANDA causes — hypertensive heart disease, rheumatic valvular disease, cardiomyopathy (incl peripartum). Echo + treat. (Cor pulmonale and TB pericarditis are separate entries.)

KDIGO 2021 Glomerular Diseases Guideline; Davidson's Principles & Practice of Medicine 24th ed (2022). Heavy proteinuria -> hypoalbuminaemia -> PERIORBITAL + generalised oedema + FROTHY urine; UGANDA causes — diabetic nephropathy, HIVAN (separate entry), primary GN (FSGS/membranous), chronic infections (HBV, schistosomiasis, malaria). Urine protein + albumin.

AASLD/EASL decompensated cirrhosis guidance; Davidson's Principles & Practice of Medicine 24th ed (2022). Hypoalbuminaemia + portal hypertension -> ASCITES (distension) + bilateral leg oedema + jaundice; UGANDA cirrhosis is often HBV +/- alcohol (schistosomal portal hypertension preserves synthetic function, so causes less oedema).

Davidson's Principles & Practice of Medicine 24th ed (2022) (chronic venous insufficiency / dependent / calcium-channel-blocker oedema). BILATERAL oedema worse by evening, no pain/redness — chronic venous insufficiency, dependent (immobility), or DRUG-INDUCED (calcium-channel blockers e.g. amlodipine — a very common, benign, reversible cause; review the medication list). NOTE: keyed on 'calcium-channel blocker' specifically — the broader 'antihypertensives' was dropped (diuretics REDUCE oedema, ACE-i/ARB do not cause it; only CCBs/vasodilators do).

weights.csoNote: CONDITIONAL on HIV/TB. UGANDA: TB pericarditis is COMMON (esp in HIV) and a leading cause of pericardial disease — EFFUSIVE (cardiac tamponade: raised JVP, pulsus paradoxus — an emergency) or CONSTRICTIVE (raised JVP + ASCITES often out of proportion to leg oedema + hepatomegaly — mimics liver disease/right HF). Raised JVP, pulsus paradoxus and pericardial knock are EXAM findings, not tokens. Echo + pericardiocentesis/ADA; anti-TB +/- steroids.
weights.weightCitation: WHO Consolidated TB Guidelines; ESC 2015 Pericardial Diseases Guideline (Adler Y et al.); Davidson's Principles & Practice of Medicine 24th ed (2022)

weights.csoNote: Right heart failure from CHRONIC LUNG DISEASE -> bilateral oedema + raised JVP. UGANDA: POST-TB LUNG DISEASE (a major legacy of the TB burden) and COPD are key causes — but 'post-TB lung disease' is not a clean token ('tuberculosis'/'TB contact' are proxies). Overlaps 'Heart failure' but flags the lung-driven RIGHT-sided mechanism; treat the lung disease + oxygen. Raised JVP is an exam finding.
weights.weightCitation: ESC; GOLD 2025; Davidson's Principles & Practice of Medicine 24th ed (2022) (cor pulmonale)

weights.csoNote: Severe chronic anaemia -> HIGH-OUTPUT cardiac failure -> bilateral oedema (with pallor + fatigue + a flow murmur). UGANDA: hookworm, malaria, nutritional/iron-deficiency and chronic-disease anaemia are common drivers — but hookworm/nutritional causes are NOT tokenised. Links to the anaemia entries in the syncope/GI-bleeding packs. Treat the anaemia + its cause.
weights.weightCitation: WHO anaemia guidance; Davidson's Principles & Practice of Medicine 24th ed (2022) (high-output failure)

weights.csoNote: CONDITIONAL on pregnancy/reproductive-age woman — a LEADING cause of maternal death in Uganda. RAPID-onset facial/generalised oedema + hypertension + proteinuria in pregnancy >20wks (or postpartum); eclampsia adds seizures. BP is in vitals; gestation/proteinuria via the obstetric flow. Management is MgSO4 + BP control + delivery; use MEOWS not NEWS2 in pregnancy. NOTE: a fixed female sexPrior was deliberately NOT used — the engine applies sexPrior to the SCORE unconditionally (pinWhen gates only the red pin), so a fixed female delta would rank pre-eclampsia highly for ALL women (incl. post-menopausal) with facial/bilateral oedema; the pregnancy/repro-age risk tokens carry the elevation instead. ('reproductive-age woman'/'missed period' are not yet capture tokens — pin currently fires on documented pregnancy.)
weights.weightCitation: WHO pre-eclampsia/eclampsia recommendations; Uganda Clinical Guidelines 2023 (obstetric); Davidson's Principles & Practice of Medicine 24th ed (2022)

weights.csoNote: Protein-energy malnutrition / HYPOALBUMINAEMIA -> bilateral (dependent + periorbital) oedema. UGANDA: from poor intake, malabsorption, or chronic wasting disease (TB, HIV, advanced cancer); 'kwashiorkor' is classically paediatric but adult hypoalbuminaemic oedema is real. Serum albumin / nutritional status is NOT tokenised — recommend a nutrition/albumin field. Treat the cause + nutritional support (cautious — refeeding).
weights.weightCitation: WHO nutrition guidance; Davidson's Principles & Practice of Medicine 24th ed (2022) (protein-energy malnutrition / hypoalbuminaemia)

weights.csoNote: Lymphatic filariasis (Wuchereria bancrofti) -> CHRONIC lymphoedema/ELEPHANTIASIS (lower limb, scrotum), typically ASYMMETRIC/unilateral, with recurrent acute lymphangitis (ADL) episodes. UGANDA: endemic in specific FOCI (not nationwide) — residence in an endemic area is the key clue, but FILARIAL exposure is not tokenised ('high-risk exposure' is a loose proxy). Non-pitting in late stages; morphology + nocturnal blood film (microfilariae) / antigen.
weights.weightCitation: WHO lymphatic filariasis guidance; Davidson's Principles & Practice of Medicine 24th ed (2022)

weights.csoNote: Acute NEPHRITIC syndrome — PERIORBITAL oedema + hypertension + HAEMATURIA (cola-coloured urine) + AKI, typically in a YOUNGER patient after a streptococcal throat/skin infection (post-infectious GN). The recent-infection history and haematuria are not cleanly tokenised. Distinguish from nephrotic (heavy proteinuria/frothy urine, less haematuria); rapidly progressive GN is an EMERGENCY. The nephritic counterpart to the nephrotic entry.
weights.weightCitation: KDIGO 2021 Glomerular Diseases Guideline; Davidson's Principles & Practice of Medicine 24th ed (2022) (acute nephritic syndrome)

weights.csoNote: UGANDA: HIV-associated nephropathy (classically collapsing FSGS) causes NEPHROTIC-range proteinuria + oedema with rapid progression to ESRD in advanced HIV — an important renal cause given the HIV burden. Large echogenic kidneys on ultrasound. A nephrotic-pattern subtype (overlaps the nephrotic-syndrome entry) flagged for the HIV population; ART improves outcomes.
weights.weightCitation: KDIGO; WHO HIV guidance; Davidson's Principles & Practice of Medicine 24th ed (2022) (HIV-associated nephropathy)

weights.csoNote: CONDITIONAL — pinned on 'Facial / laryngeal swelling' (the oed_redflags acute-angioedema capture option), NOT on the generic 'Facial / periorbital'. ACUTE facial/lip/tongue/laryngeal swelling with AIRWAY RISK — a must-not-miss emergency. Causes: ALLERGIC (food/drug/insect, +/- urticaria) or ACE-INHIBITOR-induced (bradykinin-mediated, can occur YEARS into therapy, no urticaria). ACE-inhibitor use is NOT cleanly tokenised ('antihypertensives' is a loose proxy) — recommend a specific drug token. Pin was repointed off 'Facial / periorbital' because nephrotic/AGN/HIVAN/pre-eclampsia all cause CHRONIC periorbital puffiness and would otherwise be red-flagged as angioedema (alarm fatigue); 'Facial / laryngeal swelling' is the acute red-flag option. Secure airway; stop ACE-inhibitor; allergic -> adrenaline/antihistamine/steroid.
weights.weightCitation: Davidson's Principles & Practice of Medicine 24th ed (2022) (angioedema — allergic & ACE-inhibitor-induced)
